sea.title: Two days on the Red Sea
sea.open: You are on the boat. Five scenes, one question in each. Get it right and the story takes you deeper.
beats: It is 7 am. The boat pulls out of the marina in Hurghada, the tea is already going round, and the captain turns to you with the first question of the day.
Mask on, you roll off the back of the boat. A few metres down, a flash of orange darts back into its home and watches you from inside.
You follow your guide down the reef wall. The water turns a deeper blue, and your ears start to complain.
Day two. The boat turns north toward the tip of Sinai, and your guide points at the headland ahead.
The last dive. A shape rises out of the blue below you: a ship, lying on the reef where it went down.
sea.win: You surface to the whole boat cheering. Tea is waiting on deck.

sand.title: Dune safari to camp
sand.open: The camp is somewhere past those dunes. Five questions stand between you and the fire.
beats: The tarmac ends beside a lake. Your driver steps out, kneels by the front wheel and smiles at you.
Tyres soft, engine on. The first dunes rise ahead and someone in the back asks where exactly we are.
The car drops into a wide, quiet valley. Shapes in the rock look like bones.
From the ridge the light goes fast. Phones show nothing. Your driver points up instead.
A small orange dot in the dark. Your host is already walking out to meet the car.
sand.win: You made it to camp. The fire is lit, the tea is poured, and there is a mat with your name on it.

summit.title: The night climb
summit.open: It is the middle of the night at the foot of the mountain. Five scenes, one question in each. Get it right and you climb.
beats: It is 2 am and properly cold. You switch on your torch next to old stone walls at the foot of the mountain.
Your Bedouin guide points past your summit to a darker shape against the stars, even higher than where you are going.
At a tea hut halfway up, someone warming their hands asks why on earth you all set off so early.
The air is thinner now. A friend behind you asks how much higher this mountain actually goes.
The path ends. In the torchlight a staircase of stone begins, cut by hand a long time ago.
summit.win: The sky turns pink, then gold. You are at the top, and so is everyone you climbed with.

snow.title: Up to the mountain cabin
snow.open: You are standing at the foot of a snowy mountain. Five scenes, one question in each. Get it right and you go higher, until the cabin lights come into view.
beats: The valley is quiet and cold, and the snow squeaks under your boots. First, something warm in the café.
A lift takes you above the village, swinging gently past the first pines.
You reach the tree line, where the trees thin out and the cedars and pines are heavy with snow.
The ridge is bright and windy, and a guide points to a peak far across the valley.
The last slope is steep and slow. Somewhere above, a window glows.
snow.win: Fire lit, soup on, snow falling outside. The first hot chocolate is on us.

FAVS.t: First light over Wadi El Rayan
FAVS.c: Early, before the heat, the dunes go quiet and gold. Some people sandboard. Some just sit and watch. Either way, breakfast is waiting at the bottom.

FAVS.t: The second dive at Ras Mohammed
FAVS.c: The first time under, you're thinking about your breathing. The second time, you look around. That's when the reef opens up, and most people come up asking when they can go again.
A fire, sweet tea and stories told in a dialect older than the road in. No show and no stage. It's where our name comes from, so it's part of every desert trip we run.

FAVS.t: Sunrise from the top of Mount Sinai
FAVS.c: You start in the dark, torch in hand, walking next to people you met that evening. By the time the light comes up, you're not strangers anymore.
Turquoise water so salty you can't sink. Lie back, look up and let the quiet do the rest.

FAVS.t: Pizza on the boat, between two islands
FAVS.c: Somewhere between swims, someone asks who's hungry. We make it on board, one tray at a time, with the sea still drying on your shoulders.
Baked in a clay oven and eaten straight away with honey, right next to the pottery wheels. Order a second one. You'll want it.
The chalk rocks turn silver under the moon, and the stars go all the way down to the ground. Bring a warm layer. You'll want to stay up.

FAVX: Our very first trip was here. Eleven friends, one borrowed bus, and nobody had ever stood on a sandboard. We stayed until the light went.
Am Sayed
He has opened the gate for us at dawn since that first morning, and still refuses to let anyone leave without tea.
The first time we took a group under, half the boat was scared. On the second dive the same people would not come up. That is when we knew.
Captain Hany
Twenty years on this reef. He taught most of our team how to read the water before he let us bring anyone else.
The first night we were invited to sit, we did not understand half the words. We understood the welcome. Our name comes from that fire.
Sheikh Salem
He told us what a hajeela is: going out together for the joy of it. He still pours the first glass.
Our first climb, we got the timing wrong and reached the top in the dark. We sat close and waited. Nobody has forgotten that hour.
Mousa
A Jebeliya guide who has walked this path since he was a boy. He sets the pace, and he has never left anyone behind.
The first time in Siwa, one of us lay back in the lake and went quiet for twenty minutes. We built the whole trip around that silence.
Youssef
Born in Shali. He showed us the lake that is not on the map, on the condition that we keep it slow.
The first pizza on board was a joke, made by a crew member with a small oven and a point to prove. It has been on every boat since.
Captain Mido
He still makes the first tray himself, and he still will not share the recipe.
On that first Fayoum trip we followed the smell to a clay oven and ate standing up. We have stopped there every single time since.
Om Hassan
She bakes from before sunrise. She counts our group by eye and always makes two extra.
Our first night here we forgot half the gear and did not care. Everyone slept outside the tents, just to keep looking up.
Hamada
Our camp host from the start. He taught us to switch the torches off and let our eyes adjust.

t.list.ART.a-weekend-on-a-boat: A weekend on a boat is mostly sun, salt and not much space. Pack light, pack smart, and leave the rest on shore.
t.list.ART.pack-for-the-water-not: Pack for the water, not the deck
t.list.ART.everything-you-bring-will-get: Everything you bring will get wet at some point. Soft bags, quick-dry layers and one dry set for the evening beat a big suitcase every time.
t.list.ART.sit-in-the-middle-of: Sit in the middle of the boat with your eyes on the horizon. It is the calmest seat, and it helps more than any tablet.
t.list.ART.the-deck-at-sunrise-before: The deck at sunrise, before anyone is awake
t.list.ART.masks-fins-life-jackets-and: Masks, fins, life jackets and towels are on us. Bring your own only if you love your own.
t.list.ART.bring-one-thing-that-makes: Bring one thing that makes you laugh. A card game, a speaker, a terrible hat. Boats run on mood.
t.list.ART.do-i-need-to-swim: Do I need to swim well?
t.list.ART.no-life-jackets-are-on: No. Life jackets are on board and your guide stays close.
t.list.ART.tell-your-host-early-sitting: Tell your host early. Sitting mid-ship and eating lightly helps most people.
t.list.ART.there-is-a-power-bank: There is a power bank on board, but bring your own.
t.list.ART.nothing-about-your-first-dive: Nothing about your first dive needs to be a surprise. Here is the whole thing, in the order it happens.
t.list.ART.you-sign-a-short-form: You sign a short form, try on the gear and ask every question you have. Nobody is rushing.
t.list.ART.breathing-clearing-the-mask-giv: Breathing, clearing the mask, giving a thumbs up. Knee-deep, standing up.
t.list.ART.your-instructor-is-within-arm: Your instructor is within arm’s reach. You sink a little at a time, and you equalise as you go.
t.list.ART.this-is-the-bit-people: This is the bit people remember. Fish, light, quiet. Twenty minutes feels like five.
t.list.ART.come-up-and-talk-about: Come up and talk about it
t.list.ART.tea-on-deck-everyone-talks: Tea on deck. Everyone talks at once.
t.list.ART.the-deepest-point-of-a: The deepest point of a first dive with us. Close enough to see the surface the whole time.
t.list.ART.the-first-time-under-you: The first time under, you’re thinking about your breathing. The second time, you look around.
t.list.ART.breathe-slower-than-feels-natur: Breathe slower than feels natural. Long in, longer out. It keeps you calm and makes your air last.
t.list.ART.do-i-need-to-know: Do I need to know how to swim?
t.list.ART.you-should-be-comfortable-in: You should be comfortable in water. You do not need to be fast.
t.list.ART.instructors-carry-the-safety-pl: Instructors carry the safety plan, the gear is checked daily and groups are small.
t.list.ART.give-the-signal-your-instructor: Give the signal. Your instructor brings you up, and you can try again or sit it out.
t.list.ART.the-desert-drops-fast-after: The desert drops fast after sunset. A hot afternoon and a cold night live in the same day.
t.list.ART.typical-drop-between-a-desert: Typical drop between a desert afternoon and the middle of the night. More if the sky is clear.
t.list.ART.the-camp-after-dark-one: The camp after dark, one fire and a lot of sky
t.list.ART.three-thin-layers-you-can: Three thin layers you can add or drop are warmer and easier than one heavy jacket. Wool or fleece next to the skin, a windproof on top.
t.list.ART.bring-one-more-layer-than: Bring one more layer than you think. We have blankets and a fire, but nobody ever said no to a spare hat.
t.list.ART.tents-mattresses-and-blankets-a: Tents, mattresses and blankets are on us. A warm sleeping bag is worth bringing.
t.list.ART.yes-a-simple-one-at: Yes, a simple one at camp. We will show you where.
t.list.ART.everything-important-is-include: Everything important is included. Pocket money is for the small things: a tea, a souvenir, a tip.
t.list.ART.bring-300-to-500-egp: Bring 300 to 500 EGP. A drink, something sweet and a little extra. Most people spend less than they bring.
t.list.ART.bring-500-to-800-egp: Bring 500 to 800 EGP. Extra drinks, a handmade thing from a host, and tips for guides.
t.list.ART.most-places-off-the-main: Most places off the main road do not take cards. Small notes are easier than large ones.
t.list.ART.keep-your-cash-in-two: Keep your cash in two places. A little in your pocket, the rest zipped inside your bag.
t.list.ART.entirely-optional-many-groups-p: Entirely optional. Many groups pool a tip for the guide at the end, and your host will mention it.
t.list.ART.not-sure-what-a-place: Not sure what a place costs? Ask your host in the group chat before you go. They will tell you honestly.
t.list.ART.as-listed-on-each-trip: As listed on each trip. Your trip page says exactly what is covered.
t.list.ART.for-your-booking-yes-on: For your booking, yes. On the day, bring cash.
t.list.ART.most-of-our-travellers-come: Most of our travellers come on their own. You will not be the only one, and you will not be alone for long.
t.list.ART.your-trip-has-its-own: Your trip has its own group chat. Say hello, see who is coming, and ask your host anything. By the time you leave, a few faces will already feel familiar.
t.list.ART.come-hungry-come-curious-and: Come hungry, come curious, and come as you are.
t.list.ART.your-host-introduces-everyone-i: Your host introduces everyone, in small groups and with easy questions. Nobody is put on the spot. Within an hour most people are already sharing snacks.
t.list.ART.sit-next-to-someone-new: Sit next to someone new on the bus. It is the easiest conversation you will have all week.
t.list.ART.coming-alone-and-nervous-tell: Coming alone and nervous? Tell your host. They will make sure you are never left standing at the edge of the group.
t.list.ART.will-i-be-the-only: Will I be the only solo traveller?
t.list.ART.almost-never-usually-a-third: Almost never. Usually a third of the group arrives alone.
t.list.ART.can-i-have-a-room: Can I have a room to myself?
t.list.ART.on-overnight-trips-you-can: On overnight trips you can request a private room for an extra fee.
t.list.ART.parents-ask-good-questions-here: Parents ask good questions. Here is what we tell them, so you can tell them too.
t.list.ART.a-named-host-who-travels: A named host who travels with the group the whole way. They know the place, the route and the people, and they are on the other end of the phone.
t.list.ART.overnight-trips-use-tents-cabin: Overnight trips use tents, cabins or guesthouses that we know. Rooms and bedding are listed on every trip page.
t.list.ART.first-aid-trained-hosts-small: First-aid trained hosts, small groups, check-ins during the day and a plan for bad weather. We share the full plan with any parent who asks.
t.list.ART.we-are-happy-to-talk: We are happy to talk to your family before you book. Just send us their number and a good time to call.
t.list.ART.can-my-parents-call-the: Can my parents call the host?
t.list.ART.yes-we-share-the-host: Yes. We share the host’s contact details before the trip.
t.list.ART.we-change-the-plan-not: We change the plan, not the safety. Your host decides on the day.
t.list.ART.we-do-not-just-go: We do not just go to the desert. We go with the families who live in it.
t.list.ART.a-fire-sweet-tea-and: A fire, sweet tea and stories told in a dialect older than the road in. That is how every trip starts.
t.list.ART.potters-farmers-and-a-bakery: Potters, farmers and a bakery that has not changed in forty years. You eat what they eat, in their courtyard.
t.list.ART.tea-around-the-fire-with: Tea around the fire with our hosts
t.list.ART.salt-lakes-palm-gardens-and: Salt lakes, palm gardens and a town of mud-brick houses. Your host grew up here and still lives here.
t.list.ART.bedouin-guides-who-have-walked: Bedouin guides who have walked these mountains since they were children. They carry the water, the tea and the stories.
t.list.ART.the-year-our-first-bedouin: The year our first Bedouin host family joined Hajeela. It is where our name comes from.
t.list.ART.every-host-trip-pays-the: Every host trip pays the host family directly. It is part of why they keep inviting us back.
